answer: Because the dawn stake is held until the island settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the bridge audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 28% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer burns proportionally more than endorsing a low-cost one. A farm running 180 keys therefore burns that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation trivial. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
